cohort: The study included 140 women aged 20-40 years who underwent tubal ligation and 140 women of similar age using condoms for contraception, selected from a health care center in Rudsar, Guilan Province, Iran.
finding: Women with tubal ligation experienced significantly more menstrual irregularity, polymenorrhea, hypermenorrhea, menorrhagia, and menometrorrhagia compared to women using condoms for contraception.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was significantly associated with menorrhagia (OR=2.72, CI:1.49-4.97, P=0.001).
